All650 canonical reports now use the validated v18 fingerprint and agree with the reviewed labels; triage-summary.json is complete.

- Passive JavaScript catalogs containing only immutable quoted-string initializers no longer inherit executable behavior from those unconsumed examples. Encoded-layer analysis remains available; calls, interpolation, mutation, exports and parse errors fail closed. Six unit tests passed. An inert Nx advisory string retains its known compromised commit reference while the actual malicious Nx archive still matches the hostile bootstrap control.
- The atomic finding-cap repair retains critical findings and referenced evidence needed by downstream composites/exclusions. Joined Base64 module and bounded AES-CBC/scrypt extraction expose concealed source layers; plaintext Edge.js C# bridges are parsed without compilation/execution. The bounded prefix decoder permits immediate configuration before a terminal table escape while rejecting mutation/earlier escape and preserving deferred code.

Bound behavior retains its stronger verdict. Review-omission phrasing needs an action clause before a prompt-injection consumer can use it. taxonomy-migrations.json records canonical moves.

- All-member prerequisite preflights read 807,327 members (11.56 GB) across all 650 archives, including dependencies. new-codec-v13-all-member-preflight.log/json records the result. A byte-prerequisite hit alone is not a malicious finding or a proved decoder match.

Confirmed malicious coverage:
- The Python-labelled testuser extension is byte-identical to its Marketplace archive but automatically compiles/invokes a C# Edge.js bridge. The bridge decodes shellcode, opens a Code process, allocates executable remote memory, writes it and starts a remote thread. Plaintext bridge extraction exposes existing injection and shellcode findings. Authentic registry provenance alone did not establish a benign label.
- RobloxBoard supplies a Promise.then variant of the activation-time JScript download/cscript handoff, with a namespace child-process import. Both await and completion-callback forms match, with bound writer/path/interpreter/command evidence. Different Promise objects, wrong paths, shadowed callbacks, deferred or user-command-only functions, and another script engine are negative controls. Consecutive import groups keep root-query matching bounded and avoid ambiguous sibling matching.
- Superpowers contains a Base64/AES/scrypt module appended to otherwise authentic Marketplace text-transform code; wildcard activation was also added. Static extraction exposes Solana memo-driven command execution and an encrypted Function body that launches PowerShell or curl-to-bash using memo data. The original package now has two hostile Solana findings. Authentic Marketplace source is a clear negative control; renamed array/module bindings retain detection.
- LuauConnect activation downloads a temporary JScript stage, awaits writer completion and invokes the same path through cscript. Its advertised Roblox commands are registered afterward. A bound source query detects the handoff without an endpoint, stage filename or variable-name identity gate. One hostile chain is justified. Renamed bindings and a different stage extension/address are positive controls; different writer/command paths, missing await, another script engine, an early return, a shadowed completion callback and user-command scope are negative controls.
- Checkmarx Developer Assist SHA-256 744c9d61b66bcd2bb5474d9afeee6c00bb7e0cd32535781da188b80eb59383e0 is identified by the primary incident advisory, https://checkmarx.com/blog/ongoing-security-updates/?p=108697. Static inspection proves cloud/Git authentication probes gate remote package-runner execution. Three bound hostile findings match; the bad label was reviewed and applied.
- Nx Console 18.95.0 contains the compromised GitHub bootstrap described by https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and https://nx.dev/blog/nx-console-v18-95-0-postmortem. The source's observed commit pointer is a family indicator, coupled to a real unattended GitHub task. One hostile bootstrap identity and a generic suspicious installer finding are justified; downstream payloads were not retrieved or attributed to this archive. Patched 18.100.5 matches the official package and has no suspicious/hostile findings in the prior focused rescan.
- LuaShield activation XOR-decodes an executable URL and pipes the response into a temporary native file. Its completed writer passes that same path to vscode.env.openExternal, outside the user-facing Lua obfuscation commands. The new query binds the XOR helper, key/byte array, HTTP response, writer, temporary path and OS file opener. Different file paths, ordinary PDF downloads, changed codec, shadowed callbacks, unreachable code, decrement loops and user-triggered installation are controls. A renamed/comment-free variant with a different key/address still matches. The actual downstream executable was not fetched. One visible hostile handoff chain is recorded rather than inventing its payload's capabilities.
- Earlier validated cases cover concealed extension installation, reverse shells, wallet/credential exfiltration, RC4 string-table loaders, ByteBarn encrypted job dispatch and compiled C# execution. See individual decisions for source-specific evidence and justified finding counts.

Contextual purgatory reviews:
- Modified P-language adds wildcard activation, a silent native-import IIFE and a SQLite DLL disguised as .node. Static PE inspection found no Node ABI exports, no TLS callbacks or explicit networking imports, and a trivial successful user DllMain. Two genuine suspicious findings match; hostile payload behavior remains unproved.
- Men3em agent-assistant includes actual PHP webshell examples in a skill catalog, so their hostile content findings remain visible. Reviewed selection/injection code installs skills inactive and writes toggled content into workspace instruction files. No webshell execution path was found. Purgatory is a contextual root-label decision, not suppression of the embedded hostile source. Its account-switch worker performs a user-confirmed database rewrite/relaunch.
- XAMPP manager versions expose WhatsApp QR callback material to a remote image renderer and insert message-derived database names into an unquoted shell command. Those two suspicious flows remain; local QR rendering and execFile argument arrays are negative controls.

The v11 corrections also separate GOST/cryptographic/RPC vocabulary from tunneling intent, Python standalone release references from dropper intent, ordinary debugger/minidump API sets from anti-analysis, brand-specific insecure remote-client source context from a trojan label, and unbound startup/HTTP/home-directory/JSON co-occurrence from exfiltration. A true TLS-verification-disable finding remains on the legitimate OpenLibing package. Model-branding and direct credential-privacy instructions no longer hide genuinely concealed uploads; focused adversarial controls preserve the latter finding.

Neutral taxonomy corrections retain observations and explicit consumers while removing unsupported intent. They cover administrative-operation vocabulary, registry API references, IMDS path/call co-occurrence, embedded WordPress snippets, package-runner source forms, task/state-gate context, session/deletion co-occurrence, quoted filename shell fragments, decoded Buffer-evaluation syntax and encoded URL representations. taxonomy-migrations.json records canonical IDs. Concurrent workspace migrations were reconciled without claiming authorship of their rule moves.

Registry comparisons are member-by-member, not publisher-name allowlisting. The comparison records are under /var/tmp/vsix-triage/official-comparisons. A published package can itself be compromised; provenance is combined with code review and incident evidence. HTTP 404 is never treated as proof of malice. Packaging-only differences are documented, including case-normalized documents/container XML in RobinBakshi releases, whitespace-only Snyk manifests and the platform-specific WGSL archive query. Available GDSFactory, BCAI, WillyDrucker, Godrix, Stonewolf, DeepX and GitChat releases were compared with official artifacts. Family flow audits and version deltas are retained in /var/tmp/vsix-triage/review.

All sample handling was static. No extension was installed or activated, and no sample JavaScript, script or executable was run. Network verification fetched only official registry packages and primary incident documentation; executable payload/C2 URLs were not requested.

Additional provenance checks: NexTerminal native PTY helpers differ from available official packages only in PE/debug timestamps and CodeView identifiers. Their executable code, data, unwind/relocation sections, entrypoints and layouts match; review/nexterminal-native-member-comparison.json records every differing byte class. Promptimize README bytes match after filename-case normalization, and its runtime members match. Real TLS verification-disable findings remain on Promptimize and newer Kiro SDLC releases. Registry download failures are not treated as evidence of malice.

Current additional evidence: the nineteen-package document/rendering batch includes exact OpenVSX copies of ReComment Pro, Marp and MJML. ReComment protected code was not fully reduced. Primary comparison/context artifacts: eighteenth-families-static-audit.json, eighteenth-runtime-contexts.json, eighteenth-official-deltas.json, recomment-official-readable-context.json. New live source check passed: catalog-live-cargo-check.log.

Final added malicious flow: RabobankAI.rabobank-code-assistant0.5.0 (5bbf017654190a8d1239dd0d123d884dc7db5cc523c3b6f334a6e89fa017af57) transforms a Base64 HTTPS JSON response through XChaCha20, writes and executes the same local helper at activation, and adds a global pre-commit hook that backgrounds that helper. A bound loader atom and bound Git-hook observation jointly support one hostile persistence finding; identical-condition duplicate hostile labels were removed. Renamed bindings/fields/domain/helper name and executable-mode forms are positive controls. Wrong data/path/hook, early-return, inactive and quoted-source variants are negative controls. The conservative complete-source query retains original log/comment structure; broader harmless formatting variants are not claimed. No payload was fetched or executed. Source/facts, query-generation and runtime-port notes are under /var/tmp/vsix-triage/review/rabobank-*.

JohnGaffney.blankebesxstnion1.0.2 has an activation-time buffered HTTPS JSON response whose version_hash is fixed-width hex-decoded and passed to the same child-process exec binding. The query binds the response, decoder and execution handoff, including webpack interop; renamed/namespace/quiet variants remain positive while wrong bindings, unreachable/shadowed and quoted-source variants fail. The hostile verdict comes from that flow, not the extension's name or remote address.

Quarantine limitations are explicit in decisions.json. Veldekov and Drovenko contain known GlassWorm-stage material, but the archived decoder's own-function-text guard changes decoded bytes (for example, https becomes ht4ps); ignoring that guard would invent a working payload. Ordino and three protected Windsurf account tools have unresolved startup/token flows after bounded decoder rejection. Uladluch's paired remote Gemini yolo workflow, intentionally hidden registry configuration and unverified server authorization were too uncertain for benign training; its earlier good relocation was reversed. These cases retain observed findings without padding them to a numerical suspicious target.

Microsoft's primary removal history was crosschecked against all original identities, yielding 82 matching package versions. review/microsoft-removal-review-resolutions.json records byte hashes and concrete decisions. Publisher/extension removal does not establish malware in every archived version: two HelloWorld placeholders and other local-only utilities were assessed on the actual bytes. The Cweij Sync Settings runtime differs from official Zokugun0.18.2 only by an inert activation-state timestamp/initialization block; manifest/extra dependency packaging was separately reviewed. An exact registry copy is corroborating provenance, never a blanket benign allowlist.

The last 61 decisions and protected-code limitations are in review/twentieth-review-resolutions.json. Entry points, commands, runtime snippets, selected packaged source-module contexts, official comparisons and decoder attempts are retained in twentieth-entrypoints.json, twentieth-families-static-audit.json, twentieth-account-tools.json and twentieth-protected-decoder-attempts.json under /var/tmp/vsix-triage/review. btwiuse was reviewed through its actual browser entry point: it reads a remote agents list for a status count, rather than being mislabeled inert because main is absent.

The final v18 corrections remove two remaining weak inferences: a nested client manifest describes only its own missing entry declarations, and the co-occurrence of socket, process and cryptographic markers in libsts_fixed.so establishes no backdoor. The former conjunction moved to metadata/package/entrypoint::vscode-analysis-description-without-local-entrypoint with the same matcher/exclusions; the latter redundant conjunction was retired while preserving its three existing neutral observations and has no consumers. Full Flow-Wing, its actual nested package.json, changed entry/engine manifests and the native library are controls.
